newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds bank deposits guarantee directive.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds bank deposits guarantee directive.

text.p: The European Court of Justice upheld on Tuesday the bank deposit guarantee directive enacted by the European Union Council of Ministers and rejected Germany's argument that such a law required unanimous approval.
The directive's goal is to protect depositors with credit institutions in the event the institution goes bankrupt or is unable to cover deposits, up to 20,000 Ecus.

Germany challenged the directive not because it objects to providing protection against failed banks, but because the legislation prevents Germany from offering an even more generous protection scheme outside its borders.
Germany also objected to the directive's "topping up clause" which allows foreign banks, operating in Germany but outside of its control, to match the generous German protection scheme.

Germany argued protection of depositors should be handled by each member state and that if the Community was to take this right away, it had to justify fully the reason for overriding principles of subsidiarity.
The court found the Council and the Parliament had clearly stated that the protection of small investors could only be fully guaranteed with Community level legislation.
(Original language of the case: German. Court translation into French)
